englishEquivalent: Patience is a virtue; good things come to those who wait.
literalTranslation: The patient person drinks the milk of a heifer (a young cow that has not yet given birth).
culturalContext: Rooted in Oromo pastoral wisdom: raising a young calf into a milking cow takes seasons of care. Elders use this proverb to encourage calm endurance during long journeys or hardship.

example.oromo: Hin jarjarin, obsaan aannan goromsaa dhuga.
example.english: Do not rush; with patience you will drink the heifer's milk.

englishEquivalent: Many hands make light work / No one succeeds alone.
culturalContext: Reflects the communal spirit of Daboo (mutual aid labor) and Jigii. In Oromo social ethics, mutual support is the foundation of survival and dignity.

example.oromo: Wal haa gargaarru, harki tokko hin dhiqatu.
example.english: Let us help one another; a single hand cannot wash itself.

englishEquivalent: Slow and steady wins the race.
literalTranslation: Those who walk steadily arrive safely home.
culturalContext: Cautions against reckless haste. In long highland travels across Oromia, pacing oneself ensures safe arrival before nightfall.

example.oromo: Hojii kee of eeggannoon hojjedhu; suuta deeman suuta galu.
example.english: Do your work carefully; those who walk steadily arrive safely.

englishEquivalent: Brevity is the soul of wit / Wisdom speaks concisely.
literalTranslation: The speech of a wise person is brief.
culturalContext: Under the Gadaa assembly tradition (Caffee), respected orators speak with measured clarity, avoiding boastful or empty words.

example.oromo: Yaada kee ifatti dhiyeessi; dubbiin beekaa gabaabaadha.
example.english: Present your idea clearly; a wise person's words are brief.

englishEquivalent: One tree does not make a forest / Unity is strength.
literalTranslation: A single tree does not become a forest.
culturalContext: Reminding leaders and youth alike that collective vision and solidarity create lasting shade and resilience.

example.oromo: Tokkummaan haa dhaabbannu; muki tokko bosona hin ta'u.
example.english: Let us stand in unity; one tree cannot make a forest.

englishEquivalent: Don't cry over spilt milk / Missed opportunities don't return.
literalTranslation: Water that has already flowed past cannot be scooped up.
culturalContext: Encourages forward-looking resilience and making wise decisions in the present moment rather than dwelling on past regrets.

example.oromo: Carraa har'aa fayyadami; bishaan darbe hin waraabamu.
example.english: Seize today's opportunity; water that has flowed past cannot be scooped.

englishEquivalent: Generosity brings blessings and closeness to the Divine.
literalTranslation: A generous person is close to Waaqa (God).
culturalContext: Hospitality (Keessummeessuu) is a sacred pillar of Oromo culture—welcoming travelers and strangers with buna (coffee) and food brings communal honor.

example.english: Welcome the guest; a generous person is close to God.

englishEquivalent: Knowledge is power / Education is the light of life.
literalTranslation: Learning is the light of life.
culturalContext: Celebrates lifelong learning, storytelling across generations, and passing cultural literacy from elders to diaspora and urban youth.

example.oromo: Afaan kee fi aadaa kee baradhu; barumsi ifa jireenyaati.
example.english: Learn your language and culture; education is the light of life.
